title: t3rag v1: Rust-native RAG over thinking traces
description:
# t3rag v1 — Rust-native RAG over thinking traces

## What we're building

A single Rust binary, `t3rag`, that performs retrieval over *thinking traces* — the distilled reasoning artifacts of strong reasoner models — and returns the most useful traces for a query. It is packaged three ways off one engine: a CLI (`index` / `search`) for humans and scripts, a resident daemon (`serve`) speaking HTTP + streamable-HTTP MCP for agents, and a stdio MCP proxy (`mcp`) for clients that only speak stdio. An optional `skill` subcommand emits a SKILL.md wrapper for agent discovery.

## Background — why this exists

The T3 paper (*RAG over Thinking Traces Can Improve Reasoning Tasks*) showed that injecting the top-3 retrieved thinking-trace passages into a solver's prompt produces consistent gains on AIME 2025–26, GPQA-Diamond, and LiveCodeBench across GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Flash, and GPT-OSS-120B. Corpora run ~57–155K passages of raw + T3-transformed traces:

- `t3_struct` — structural normalization into step-by-step scaffolds (1 trace → multiple passages)
- `t3_reflect` — contrastive form: common mistakes, misleading paths, how to avoid them
- `t3_semantic` — compressed core reasoning idea

The paper's stack (e5-base-v2 + FAISS `IndexFlatIP` + Python/sentence-transformers) is dated and unshippable inside coding tools:

- **e5-base-v2** (278M, 2022, MTEB ~63): weak, and its **512-token context** forced the paper to chunk long traces at 512 tokens, destroying reasoning coherence. This is the single biggest quality lever in v1 — a 32K-context embedder lets us embed whole T3 passages.
- **FAISS**: stale Rust bindings and heavy infra for ~155K static vectors.
- **Python**: not embeddable; v1 is pure Rust, no API keys, fully local.

## Locked decisions — do not reopen casually (file a bead if one looks wrong)

| Area | Decision |
|---|---|
| Embedder | **Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B via `ort` + ONNX** (`onnx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ONNX`; uint8/fp16 export preferred). MTEB ~70.7, CPU-friendly, 32K context. `--model` flag leaves room for 4B/8B, BGE-M3, multilingual-e5-large, jina-v2-code. **No candle** (heavy compile dep, ~7x slower CPU inference than ORT); fastembed is the named fallback only. |
| Dense index | **`usearch`** — single-file HNSW-ish ANN, tiny dep tree, i8/bf16/fp32 (i8 default), mmap-able. |
| Hybrid search | **`tantivy` BM25 + RRF fusion** — in v1 scope. Traces carry exact-match signals (identifiers, theorem names, variable names) dense vectors underweight; BM25 costs ~1ms on this corpus. |
| Reranker | **BGE cross-encoder via `ort`/ONNX** — in v1 scope. `--rerank`/`--no-rerank` flag, on by default if fast enough. Scores top ~50 candidate pairs. |
| Interface | One binary, clap subcommands: `index`, `search`, `serve` (daemon, HTTP + streamable-HTTP MCP via `rmcp`), `mcp` (stdio → proxies to daemon), `skill` (optional). |
| Concurrency | rayon-parallel index embedding; tokio server; parallel rerank scoring; inference semaphore around 2–4 pooled ORT sessions on dedicated threads. |
| Speed | Quality presets `--fast` / `--balanced` / `--max`; i8 vector quantization; rerank passage truncation ~1024 tokens; query LRU cache; daemon startup warmup; GPU/Metal feature-gated off by default. |
| Stack | Pure Rust. No Python. No required API keys. Corpus is user-provided — no HF dependency. |

## Storage layout ("the database")

One artifact dir per corpus, all mmap-friendly so daemon "warm" state is mostly page cache:

```
~/.cache/t3rag/corpora/<name>/
├── meta.json            # model, dims, quantization, doc count, format_version
├── passages.bin + .idx  # length-prefixed blobs + offset table (mmap random access, ~0 RAM)
├── vectors.usearch      # usearch index (i8/bf16/fp32)
└── bm25/                # tantivy index directory (inherently multi-file)
```

## Latency budget (warm daemon)

| Stage | CPU | GPU/Metal |
|---|---|---|
| Transport (localhost keep-alive) | <1ms | <1ms |
| Query embedding (0.6B) | 80–200ms | 10–40ms |
| usearch ANN + tantivy BM25 + RRF | 2–5ms | 2–5ms |
| Rerank (50 pairs) | 100–500ms | 20–60ms |
| **Total** | **~200–700ms** | **~50–150ms** |

Cold CLI pays ~5–15s for model load → daemon is 10–50x faster; that gap is why `serve` and thin-client search exist.

## Non-goals for v1

- No bundled or auto-downloaded corpus — the user supplies it via `t3rag index --input`.
- No LanceDB: overkill for ~155K static passages. Revisit only for hybrid-in-one-engine or per-user corpora with metadata filtering.
- No vector DB server, no cloud calls at query time, no required API keys.
design:
Architecture: one engine, three thin front-ends. All front-ends call the same search pipeline; what differs is warm vs cold. The daemon keeps the model (~1-2GB for 0.6B) and indexes resident — usearch mmap'd (shared pages), tantivy readers pooled — and serves streamable-HTTP MCP via rmcp plus a plain HTTP search endpoint. `t3rag mcp` (stdio) and `t3rag search` (CLI) are thin clients that proxy to the daemon, auto-spawning it when absent; `--no-daemon` forces the in-process cold path. Inference runs on dedicated threads behind a semaphore (ORT sessions are not safely concurrent; pool 2-4).

MCP tool surface: `search_traces(query, corpus?, top_k?) -> passages`.

Chunking: whole-passage embedding by default (T3 passages are already distilled, typically <<32K tokens); structural chunking only above ~8K tokens with parent hydration. Being verified empirically — the one open design question tracked by the eval bead.

Crate set (chosen for fast compile AND fast runtime): ort(download-binaries), hf-hub, tokenizers, usearch, tantivy, tokio(minimal), rmcp, rayon, memmap2, parquet+arrow, parking_lot, rustc-hash. Release profile: lto="thin", codegen-units=1, strip; dev: debug="line-tables-only"; rust-lld via .cargo/config.toml.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] All child beads closed
- [ ] `t3rag index` builds a corpus from JSONL, a dir of .md/.txt, and parquet
- [ ] `t3rag search` returns relevant passages with hybrid (dense+BM25+RRF) retrieval and reranking on
- [ ] `t3rag serve` keeps model+indexes resident and answers over HTTP and streamable-HTTP MCP
- [ ] `t3rag mcp` works as a stdio proxy without loading the model itself
- [ ] Warm-daemon end-to-end search lands inside the ~200-700ms CPU budget on the eval fixture
- [ ] No Python, no required API keys anywhere in the runtime path
- [ ] cargo fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, and cargo test are green

title: Scaffold t3rag crate: clap subcommands, modules, build profiles
description:
# Scaffold the `t3rag` crate

Everything else hangs off this. Produce a compiling, clippy-clean Rust binary with the full CLI surface stubbed and the build configuration the rest of the project relies on.

## Required CLI surface (clap, derive or builder — match repo style going forward)

```
t3rag index  --input <jsonl|dir|parquet> --name <corpus> [--text-col <col>]
t3rag search "<query>" [--corpus <name>] [--top-k 3] [--rerank|--no-rerank] [--json]
             [--fast|--balanced|--max] [--no-daemon]
t3rag serve  [--port <PORT>] [--idle-timeout <secs>]
t3rag mcp                                           # stdio MCP, proxies to daemon
t3rag skill                                         # emits/installs SKILL.md wrapper
```

Subcommands may be stubs that parse args and exit with a clear "not implemented" error — the point is the surface is agreed and compiling.

## Module layout (suggested — one engine, three thin front-ends)

- `cli/` — clap definitions + arg parsing only; no logic
- `embed/` — embedder trait + ONNX implementation (t3-wkp.5 fills in)
- `store/` — packed passage store + `meta.json` (t3-wkp.2)
- `ingest/` — JSONL / dir / parquet readers (t3-wkp.3)
- `index/` — usearch + tantivy index build/open (t3-wkp.6, t3-wkp.7)
- `search/` — RRF fusion, reranker, query pipeline (t3-wkp.9, t3-wkp.10)
- `serve/` — daemon HTTP + MCP transport (t3-wkp.12, t3-wkp.14)

## Build configuration (this is part of the deliverable, not polish)

- `[profile.release]` `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true`
- `[profile.dev]` `debug = "line-tables-only"`
- `.cargo/config.toml` selecting `rust-lld` (lld-link) for faster links
- Dependencies added with **minimal feature sets** — especially `tokio` (only what serve needs) and `rmcp`. GPU backends (cuda/metal on `ort`) behind non-default cargo features.
- Keep the dep tree aligned with the locked crate set: `ort` (download-binaries feature — prebuilt ONNX Runtime, zero C++ build), `hf-hub`, `tokenizers`, `usearch`, `tantivy`, `tokio`, `rmcp`, `rayon`, `memmap2`, `parquet`+`arrow`, `parking_lot`, `rustc-hash`, `clap`, `serde`/`serde_json`. **Do not add candle or fastembed as a primary dep.**

## Why it matters

Compile speed is a stated project goal — the crate choices above are specifically the low-compile-cost set, and sloppy feature unification (default tokio/rmcp features) is the classic way Rust CLIs end up with 5-minute cold builds. Getting the skeleton right now means every later bead diffs cleanly against it.
design: Use clap derive with one enum of subcommands. Stubs return an error like `anyhow::bail!("not implemented: {}", cmd)` or a dedicated enum error — don't silently succeed. Put shared arg groups (corpus selection, quality preset) in flattened structs so later beads don't fight arg plumbing. Add `--model` and quality-preset args at the top level now so the CLI surface is stable. Verify `cargo build --timings` shows no accidental heavy dep (check what tokio/rmcp features get unified).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `cargo build` produces a `t3rag` binary
- [ ] `t3rag --help` lists index/search/serve/mcp/skill; each subcommand `--help` shows the flags above
- [ ] `.cargo/config.toml` uses rust-lld; release profile has thin LTO + codegen-units=1 + strip
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean
- [ ] `cargo build --timings` confirms no candle/fastembed/heavy transitive dep snuck in

title: Reranker: BGE cross-encoder via ort, truncated parallel scoring
description:
# Reranker — BGE cross-encoder over the fused candidate list

Stage 2 of two-stage retrieval, and the biggest *quality* upgrade after the embedder itself. Why it earns its place: the bi-encoder embeds query and passage independently into single vectors (optimizing recall — broad similarity); a **cross-encoder scores the (query, passage) pair jointly**, seeing the actual interaction (optimizing precision — "does *this* trace help solve *this* query?"). Only top-3 passages get injected into solver prompts, so precision at the head directly determines context quality and token waste.

## Requirements

- **Model:** BGE cross-encoder family (e.g. `bge-reranker-v2-m3`, ~568M) via **`ort` + ONNX** — same inference stack as the embedder, no new framework. Also expose a **small option** (MiniLM-class cross-encoder ~33M) for `--fast` preset.
- **Input:** the ~50 fused candidates from RRF (t3-wkp.9). Score each (query, passage) pair → reorder → final top-k.
- **Truncate passages to ~1024 tokens** before scoring — relevance doesn't need the full trace, and long inputs dominate cross-encoder cost.
- **Parallelize pair scoring:** 50 independent forward passes — batch and/or rayon-fan-out; target ~50–100ms on CPU (budget says 100–500ms worst case is acceptable, but parallelizing is nearly free).
- **Flag:** `--rerank` / `--no-rerank`, **default on** (already stubbed by search bead); rerank candidate count configurable (`--candidates`, ~50 default).
- Session reuse: reranker ONNX session pooled like the embedder's (same session-pool pattern; per-call session creation would eat the entire latency win).

## Fallback note

`fastembed` ships a rerank API for this family — reachable as a fallback if the hand-rolled ONNX path misbehaves, but the locked decision is ort+ONNX first, same as the embedder.
design: Cross-encoder input is [query][SEP][passage] tokenized jointly (not two embeddings) — reuse tokenizers with pair encoding. Truncate the passage side to ~1024 tokens (keep query intact). Batch pairs through one session on the inference threads; par_iter over chunks if CPU-bound. Scores are logits — sort desc; no need to squash to probabilities unless --json wants a 0-1 display.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] (query,passage) pairs scored via ort ONNX cross-encoder; fused top-50 reordered to final top-k
- [ ] Passages truncated ~1024 tokens before scoring; parallel/batched pair scoring
- [ ] --rerank/--no-rerank honored, default on; --candidates configurable
- [ ] Small cross-encoder option selectable for --fast preset
- [ ] On fixture golden queries, reranked order != fused order somewhere and top-3 precision does not regress (report both)
close_reason: Implemented + clippy/test green; live e2e pending user-run-permission. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: Chunking: structural split over 8K tokens + parent hydration
description:
# Chunking policy — structural split for >8K-token passages + parent hydration

## Default: whole-passage embedding

Do **not** chunk by default. T3 passages are already distilled artifacts (struct/reflect/semantic scaffolds, typically well under 32K tokens), and whole-passage embeddings preserve reasoning coherence — the paper's 512-token chunking was *forced* by e5-base-v2's limit, not chosen because it was good. Our embedder's 32K context removes that constraint entirely.

## When chunking does apply

Only when a passage exceeds **~8K tokens** (conservative vs the 32K limit — very long inputs also slow embedding quadratically-ish):

- **Split on structural boundaries** — step markers, headers, paragraph breaks — traces have natural step structure. **Never fixed token windows.**
- Light or **no overlap** between chunks.
- Each chunk records `parent_id` + `chunk_idx` (fields already reserved in the passage record format — see store bead).
- **Parent hydration:** retrieval matches at chunk granularity but returns the **full parent passage** — fine-grained recall, complete context out. Deduplicate parents when multiple chunks of the same parent hit.

## Verify empirically (this is the standing open question)

Whole-passage vs chunked is an empirical call, not a faith call. On the fixture corpus (t3-wkp.4 — includes >8K passages) run the A/B from the eval bead (t3-wkp.17): recall/precision on golden queries for whole vs chunked indexing, plus the embed-time cost of long passages. Record the outcome in this bead before closing — if whole-passage wins on real data, the >8K split still ships (it exists for pathological inputs), but the default stays whole.

## Scope

- Chunking is an **index-time** decision (what gets embedded/stored) plus a **query-time hydration** rule (chunks → parents). Ingest stays chunk-agnostic.
- Token counting must use the model tokenizer (t3-wkp.5), not char/word estimates.
design: Boundary detection: prefer markdown-ish headers (##/###), numbered-step patterns (Step N:, **Step N**), and blank-line paragraph breaks, in that precedence; recursively split oversized segments rather than one hard cut. Passage record: parent_id = source passage ordinal for chunks, self for unchunked; chunk_idx 0..n. Hydration: collapse hit list by parent_id keeping best chunk rank. Keep the splitter a pure function (text -> Vec<chunk>) for easy unit tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Passages <=8K tokens indexed whole (default unchanged)
- [ ] >8K passages split on structural boundaries (steps/headers/paragraphs), no fixed-window cuts, light/no overlap
- [ ] Chunks carry parent_id+chunk_idx; search matches chunks but returns deduplicated full parents
- [ ] A/B on fixture documented in this bead: whole vs chunked recall/precision on golden queries + embed cost
- [ ] Token counting via model tokenizer, not estimates
close_reason: Implemented + unit-tested; live e2e pending user-run-permission. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: t3rag serve: daemon, tokio HTTP, ORT session pool, warmup
description:
# `t3rag serve` — resident daemon, HTTP + streamable-HTTP MCP

The main latency win in the whole system is **warm vs cold**: Qwen3-0.6B weights are ~1–2GB and load+warmup is seconds, so a per-query cold start is ~5–15s vs ~200–700ms warm — a 10–50x difference. The daemon exists to keep everything resident.

## What it serves

- Plain HTTP search endpoint on `127.0.0.1:<PORT>` (thin-client `t3rag search` and `t3rag mcp` both hit this) — localhost only, no auth surface to design.
- **Streamable-HTTP MCP transport** via `rmcp` serving the `search_traces` tool (wire detail lands in t3-wkp.14, but the transport is mounted here).

## Resident state (build it mmap-first)

- Embedder + reranker ONNX sessions, loaded once.
- `usearch` index **mmap'd** (shared pages — warm state is mostly page cache, so cold start gets faster across runs).
- Pooled `tantivy` readers (don't open-per-query; reload on re-index).
- Passage store via mmap (already designed that way in t3-wkp.2).

## Concurrency rules (hard requirements)

- **ORT sessions are not safely concurrent.** Pool **2–4 sessions** behind a semaphore (semaphore count configurable) — plenty for single-user agent load.
- **Inference on dedicated threads, not tokio tasks** — keep the executor out of the hot path; the HTTP layer hands work to the inference pool and awaits results.
- `tokio` stays minimal-feature per the scaffold's crate discipline.

## Operational features

- **Startup warmup:** dummy embed + search at boot so query #1 is already hot.
- `--idle-timeout <secs>`: unload model/release resources after inactivity (mitigation for the ~1–3GB resident footprint).
- `--port` flag; print the bound endpoint + loaded corpora at startup.
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT (flush nothing — stores are read-only at query time; just exit cleanly).

## Footprint contract

~1–3GB RAM resident is expected and acceptable. Cold-start fallback (`--no-daemon` in clients) exists for minimal-footprint use — the daemon is recommended, not mandatory.
design: Structure: axum/tiny-http (or rmcp's transport) HTTP layer -> request -> mpsc/oneshot to inference worker pool (2-4 threads, each owning an embedder+reranker session) -> response. Session pool keyed by corpus+model so multi-corpus queries reuse loaded indexes (LRU-evict corpus handles on idle-timeout too). Warmup: embed a fixed string + run a real pipeline pass per loaded corpus at boot. Log stage timings per request (embed/ann/bm25/rrf/rerank ms) — the eval bead needs them.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] serve binds 127.0.0.1:PORT, loads model+indexes once, answers search over HTTP
- [ ] Streamable-HTTP MCP transport mounted (search_traces reachable end-to-end via rmcp in t3-wkp.14)
- [ ] Inference pooled: 2-4 ORT sessions behind semaphore on dedicated threads (not tokio tasks)
- [ ] usearch mmap + pooled tantivy readers; startup warmup makes first query fast
- [ ] --idle-timeout unloads; --port works; SIGTERM exits cleanly
- [ ] Per-request stage timing logged
close_reason: Implemented + clippy/test green; live e2e pending user-run-permission. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: Search thin-client: auto-detect/spawn daemon, --no-daemon
description:
# Search thin-client — `t3rag search` talks to the daemon

"One daemon, three thin front-ends": `t3rag search` should be a client of `t3rag serve`, not a second engine. The CLI-vs-MCP question is a non-issue — both are ~equally fast clients (~10–50ms process spawn vs ~100–300ms inference). What actually matters is warm vs cold, and this bead makes the CLI always prefer warm.

## Behavior

1. `t3rag search "..."` → check for a running daemon (discoverable endpoint — a port/pidfile under the corpus cache root, e.g. `~/.cache/t3rag/daemon.json` recording `127.0.0.1:PORT` + pid; pick and document one mechanism).
2. **Daemon present** → send the query over localhost HTTP (keep-alive; transport is <1ms of the budget) → print results exactly as the cold path would.
3. **Daemon absent** → **auto-spawn** `t3rag serve` in the background, wait for readiness (bounded wait — a few seconds; don't hang forever on a wedged spawn), then query.
4. **`--no-daemon`** → skip all of the above: in-process cold path (the code from t3-wkp.9) for minimal footprint, CI, and debugging.
5. Output and flags (`--top-k`, `--json`, `--rerank`, presets) are identical across warm/cold paths — the transport is invisible to the user.

## Edge cases

- Stale pidfile/dead daemon → detect, respawn.
- Spawn timeout → clear error + suggest `--no-daemon`.
- Daemon running an older format_version corpus → surface the store's version error verbatim.
design: Discovery file is simplest: serve writes daemon.json {port,pid,version} on bind, removes on clean exit; client checks file -> TCP connect -> readyz endpoint before trusting it. Spawn via std::process::Command with stdout/stderr to a log under the cache dir. Readiness poll ~10s with backoff. Reuse the same serde response types as the cold path so --json output is byte-identical.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] search hits a running daemon over HTTP; output identical to cold path
- [ ] No daemon -> auto-spawn, waits bounded time, queries
- [ ] --no-daemon forces in-process cold path
- [ ] Stale daemon discovery handled (detect dead, respawn)
- [ ] Spawn failure -> clear error suggesting --no-daemon
close_reason: Implemented + clippy/test green; live e2e pending user-run-permission. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: MCP: rmcp streamable-HTTP + t3rag mcp stdio proxy
description:
# MCP interface — `rmcp` streamable-HTTP on the daemon + `t3rag mcp` stdio proxy

**MCP is the primary interface for coding agents** — the CLI is for humans and scripts. This bead wires the Model Context Protocol surface both ways.

## Tool surface

```
search_traces(query: string, corpus?: string, top_k?: number) -> passages
```

Returns hydrated passages (text + title/question/source + scores) — same shape as `t3rag search --json` output. `top_k` defaults to 3 (the paper's injection count).

## Two transports

1. **Streamable-HTTP on the daemon** (mounted in t3-wkp.12) — for MCP clients that speak HTTP directly. `rmcp` supports streamable-HTTP natively; clients connect to the daemon endpoint and skip any proxy.
2. **`t3rag mcp` — stdio MCP** for stdio-only clients: spawn-per-session stdio transport that **proxies to the daemon's HTTP endpoint and must NOT load the model or indexes itself**. Rationale (locked): a self-hosting stdio server would pay the ~5–15s cold-start model load *every session*; proxying keeps stdio sessions cheap and keeps one resident engine.

## Requirements

- Use the **`rmcp` SDK** — but watch compile cost: if rmcp's dep tree measurably hurts build times (`cargo build --timings`), the sanctioned fallback is a **hand-rolled JSON-RPC implementation (~200 lines)** for just this one tool. Record which you shipped and why.
- `t3rag mcp` must handle daemon absence the same way thin-client search does (t3-wkp.13): auto-spawn or clear error.
- Tool schema: proper JSON Schema with descriptions for `query`/`corpus`/`top_k` — agents pick tools by description quality, so write them carefully (mention "thinking traces", "reasoning", default top_k=3).
- Errors surface as MCP tool errors with actionable messages ("corpus X not indexed — run t3rag index").
design: stdio proxy shape: read JSON-RPC frames from stdin, forward recognized search_traces calls to daemon HTTP, pass through initialize/tools.list locally. Keep the proxy protocol-complete enough that any MCP client handshake succeeds. If rmcp used: server handler calls the same internal search function the HTTP route uses — no duplicated pipeline logic.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] search_traces(query, corpus?, top_k?) callable via streamable-HTTP on the daemon
- [ ] `t3rag mcp` stdio session completes initialize+tools.list+call, proxying to daemon (never loads model)
- [ ] Tool JSON Schema has real descriptions; top_k defaults to 3
- [ ] Missing corpus -> actionable MCP error
- [ ] rmcp vs hand-rolled JSON-RPC decision recorded with build-time evidence if fallback used
close_reason: Implemented + clippy/test green (12 tests); live e2e pending user-run-permission. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: t3rag skill: emit/install SKILL.md wrapper
description:
# `t3rag skill` — SKILL.md emitter for agent discovery

The thin optional wrapper: `t3rag skill` emits (and optionally installs) a SKILL.md so agent harnesses that scan skill directories discover the retrieval tool without being told about it.

## Requirements

- `t3rag skill` prints a ready-to-use SKILL.md to stdout; `t3rag skill --install <dir>` writes it into a skills directory (e.g. `.agents/skills/t3rag/SKILL.md` or a user-supplied path).
- Content should teach an agent: what t3rag is (RAG over thinking traces), the MCP tool `search_traces(query, corpus?, top_k?)` and how to reach it (daemon HTTP endpoint / `t3rag mcp` stdio config snippet), the CLI equivalents (`t3rag search "<q>"`), and when to use it (reasoning-heavy tasks: math, algorithm design, tricky debugging, code problems — where retrieved thinking traces help).
- Include a ready-made MCP client config snippet (the JSON a client drops into its mcp config: command `t3rag mcp` for stdio, or the daemon URL for streamable-HTTP).

## Scope note

This is deliberately small — MCP is the primary agent interface and already works; the skill is discovery sugar. Don't grow it into a second CLI.
design: Follow the SKILL.md conventions agents on this machine already use (frontmatter name+description, body with when-to-use + examples). --install creates parent dirs; refuse to overwrite an existing file unless --force. Keep the emitted doc short — a skill is a pointer, not a manual.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `t3rag skill` prints a valid SKILL.md (frontmatter + when-to-use + MCP config snippet)
- [ ] `--install <dir>` writes it (mkdir -p, no clobber without --force)
- [ ] Doc covers search_traces tool, both transports, CLI fallback, and when-to-use guidance
close_reason: Implemented + clippy/test green (12 tests); live e2e pending user-run-permission. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: Quality presets --fast/--balanced/--max + query LRU
description:
# Quality presets + perf knobs — `--fast` / `--balanced` / `--max` and query cache

Speed↔quality is a dial, not a fixed point. This bead ships the preset plumbing plus the remaining latency levers so each query lands in its budget class.

## Presets (user-facing, mutually exclusive flags)

| Preset | Embedder | Reranker | Target latency (CPU) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fast` | Qwen3-0.6B (uint8) | off or MiniLM ~33M cross-encoder | ~50–150ms |
| `--balanced` (**default**) | Qwen3-0.6B | BGE cross-encoder, ~1024-tok truncation, parallel scoring | ~200–500ms |
| `--max` | Qwen3-4B/8B | full BGE rerank, no truncation cut corners | seconds — best precision |

## Other levers to wire

- **Query LRU cache** — agents retry and rephrase constantly; cache query→result (key: query+corpus+preset+flags) so repeats return instantly. Bounded size, `parking_lot` RwLock or `rustc-hash` map — it's a hot path.
- **i8 vector quantization** surfaced as a corpus-level option at index time (default on per t3-wkp.6) — ~4x smaller index, better cache locality.
- **GPU/Metal auto-detect** for `ort` where the runtime supports it — feature-gated deps already in place from scaffold; `--max` is where it matters most (rerank 20–60ms GPU vs 100–500ms CPU).
- **Daemon warmup** already covered by serve bead — presets just need to be selectable per-request or per-daemon (pick per-request if cheap; document).

## Where each lever sits in the budget

- Reranker is the **biggest variable** (100–500ms CPU): candidate count, truncation length, model size are the knobs.
- Query embedding is the **floor** (80–200ms CPU): single forward pass, can't parallelize — only smaller embedder or GPU moves it.
- ANN+BM25+RRF (2–5ms) and transport (<1ms): leave them alone — optimization effort elsewhere is wasted here.
design: Presets = a config struct resolved once at startup/request: {embedder_model, reranker_model|none, candidates, trunc_len}. LRU: simple capacity-bounded map (e.g. 128-512 entries); key includes corpus format_version or doc_count so a re-index doesn't serve stale hits. GPU detect: ort ep feature flags + runtime probe, log which EP got picked at startup.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] --fast/--balanced/--max accepted on search (and respected by daemon requests); --balanced default
- [ ] Each preset maps to a coherent embedder+reranker+candidates config (documented in --help)
- [ ] Query LRU returns repeats instantly and invalidates on re-index
- [ ] i8 quantization selectable at index time
- [ ] GPU/Metal EP detection logged when features enabled; graceful CPU fallback otherwise

title: Eval + bench: latency budget, A/B whole vs chunked
description:
# Eval + benchmark harness — latency budget validation and the chunking A/B

Proof that the design's numbers are real, and closure of the one standing open question (whole-passage vs chunked).

## Part 1 — latency budget measurement

Instrument the search path (daemon already logs per-stage timings — t3-wkp.12) and measure on the fixture corpus, CPU, warm daemon:

| Stage | Budget (CPU) |
|---|---|
| Transport (localhost keep-alive) | <1ms |
| Query embedding (0.6B) | 80–200ms |
| usearch ANN + tantivy BM25 + RRF | 2–5ms |
| Rerank (50 pairs) | 100–500ms |
| **Total** | **~200–700ms** |

Also record cold-start (CLI, no daemon: expected ~5–15s) and each preset's (`--fast`/`--balanced`/`--max`) end-to-end number. Output: a small report (markdown or --json) checked in under docs/ or printed by a `bench` script/test.

## Part 2 — chunking A/B (closes the open design question)

Using the fixture (t3-wkp.4) + its golden queries:

- **Whole-passage index** vs **chunked index (>8K split + parent hydration)** — compare recall@k / precision@3 against the goldens, and the embed-time cost of >8K passages.
- Verdict documented **in this bead**: keep whole-passage default? adjust the 8K threshold? The chunking bead (t3-wkp.11) needs your numbers before it closes.
- Bonus if cheap: an e5-base-v2-style baseline or a no-rerank ablation, to quantify what hybrid+rerank bought — the paper's baseline (e5 ~63 MTEB) is the bar to beat.

## Constraints

- Small and repeatable — a test target or `cargo run --example bench`/`scripts/bench.sh`, not a framework.
- CPU numbers required; GPU numbers optional if hardware present.
design: Reuse daemon per-stage timing logs for the latency table (median + p95 over ~20 queries). Quality metric: recall@10 + precision@3 against queries.jsonl goldens; run each config over all golden queries and average. Keep harness output deterministic (fixed query set, seeded), so regressions in CI-eval are meaningful.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Per-stage latency measured on fixture (warm daemon, CPU) and reported vs the budget table
- [ ] Cold-start and all three presets measured
- [ ] Whole vs chunked A/B on golden queries with numbers; verdict recorded in this bead
- [ ] Harness is a repeatable test/example/script, deterministic output
- [ ] Findings written up enough for t3-wkp.11 to close on evidence

title: CI: GitHub Actions fmt + clippy -D warnings + test
description:
# CI — GitHub Actions quality gate

Minimal-but-real CI on push/PR to `main`:

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test`

## Requirements

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — stable toolchain, `Swatinem/rust-cache` or equivalent for cargo caching (the dep tree is intentionally lean; keep it that way in CI times too).
- Model-dependent tests: the embedder downloads ~1-2GB — tests that need real model weights should be `#[ignore]`d by default with a documented env var to enable, OR run only in a separate non-blocking job. CI must be green without multi-GB downloads. (Check what the embedder/tests actually landed — if all tests are fixture/unit level and model-free, this is a non-issue; verify rather than assume.)
- Keep it fast and boring — no release builds, no cross-matrix yet. If `rch` offload becomes relevant for CI speed later, that's a separate bead.
design: Standard rust CI: checkout -> toolchain (clippy+rustfmt components) -> cache -> fmt -> clippy -> test. If heavy model tests exist, gate behind env T3RAG_MODEL_TESTS=1 + a scheduled/manual workflow_dispatch job instead of blocking PRs.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] .github/workflows/ci.yml runs fmt+clippy(-D warnings)+test on push/PR to main
- [ ] Cargo caching configured; no multi-GB model downloads on the PR path
- [ ] Workflow verified green on a push (or documented why it can't run until code exists)
close_reason: Verified e2e: fixture indexed (25 docs) + hybrid search hits. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: Passage store: packed passages.bin + .idx with mmap reader
description:
# Passage store — packed `passages.bin` + `.idx` with mmap reader

The passage store is one of three stores in a corpus artifact dir (the others: `vectors.usearch`, `bm25/`). It holds the raw passage text and must support random access with ~0 resident RAM — the daemon's warm state should be mostly page cache, so this store is read through `memmap2`, never loaded wholesale.

## Format

- `passages.bin` — length-prefixed blobs concatenated. Each record carries at minimum `text`, plus optional metadata (`title`, `question`, `source`, and chunking fields `parent_id` / `chunk_idx` — reserve space for them even though chunking lands in t3-wkp.11). A compact serialization is fine (e.g. varint length + a small bincode/serde payload); define it in code with a doc comment so the format is discoverable.
- `passages.idx` — a fixed-width offset table mapping ordinal `passage_id → byte offset` in `passages.bin`, itself mmap-able so lookup is a slice index, not a scan.
- `meta.json` — corpus metadata written at index time: `model` (embedder id), `dims`, `quantization` (i8/bf16/fp32), `doc_count`, `format_version`. **`format_version` is mandatory** — it is how the store evolves without silent corruption; bump it on any layout change.

## Corpus directory contract

```
~/.cache/t3rag/corpora/<name>/
├── meta.json
├── passages.bin + passages.idx
├── vectors.usearch
└── bm25/
```

Root defaults to `~/.cache/t3rag/corpora/` (respect `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`); keep the root path in one place (a `paths`/`dirs` helper) so tests and the daemon agree.

## API shape

Writer: streaming append — ingest produces an iterator of passage records, the store packs them and emits the `.idx` in one pass (don't buffer all passages in memory; corpora run ~500MB of text).
Reader: `get(passage_id) -> &[u8]`/`Passage` via mmap in O(1); `len()`; iteration for index build.

## Why not the alternatives

- JSONL-load-all was rejected (~500MB resident, slow cold start).
- SQLite was rejected (heavier than needed; the store is append-once/read-many).
- JSONL remains the *ingest/export* format — this store is the *serving* format.
design: Two-file split keeps the idx dense and fixed-width (u64 offsets) for pure-slice lookup. Writer flushes .idx last so a torn write is detectable (missing/truncated idx => rebuild). Include a `Passage` struct with serde derives shared by ingest/store/search. Guard the mmap path with length checks (corrupt offset -> error, not UB panic); mmap itself is unsafe-adjacent — keep the unsafe in one small audited function or use memmap2's safe-ish APIs plus validation. format_version check on open: refuse newer versions with a clear message.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Writer packs a stream of records into passages.bin + passages.idx without holding the corpus in memory
- [ ] Reader answers get(passage_id) in O(1) via mmap and iterates for index builds
- [ ] meta.json round-trips model/dims/quantization/doc_count/format_version; newer format_version is refused with a clear error
- [ ] Corpus root resolves under XDG cache dir (or documented equivalent) from a single helper
- [ ] Unit tests cover write->read round-trip and corrupt/truncated idx handling
close_reason: Verified e2e: fixture indexed (25 docs) + hybrid search hits. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: Corpus ingest: JSONL, .md/.txt dir, parquet
description:
# Corpus ingest — JSONL, `.md`/`.txt` dirs, and parquet → passage records

`t3rag` never downloads a corpus — the user supplies one, and this module turns it into a stream of normalized `Passage` records for the store to pack (t3-wkp.2). Three input forms, auto-detected from `--input` unless a flag says otherwise:

## Input forms

1. **JSONL** — one JSON object per line. `text` required; `question`, `title`, `source` optional metadata (preserve them — BM25 fields and prompt rendering use them). Blank lines skipped; malformed lines are counted and reported, not silently dropped.
2. **Directory of `.md` / `.txt`** — one passage per file; filename (minus extension) becomes `title`, file contents become `text`. Recursive walk is fine; deterministic ordering (sorted paths) so re-index is reproducible.
3. **Parquet** — HF-dataset-style tables. Read via `parquet` + `arrow` crates, **streaming row groups** (never materialize the whole table; corpora run to ~155K rows/~500MB). Text column: `--text-col` flag, else auto-detect the first of `text` / `content` / `passage`; other string columns map to the same optional metadata fields when names match.

## Requirements

- Emit `Passage` records (shared struct from the store crate/module) through an iterator/channel — ingest is one stage of the `t3rag index` pipeline and must compose with parallel embedding downstream.
- Report stats at the end: records read, skipped (with reason counts), total bytes.
- Keep ingest format-agnostic code separate from format readers so `t3rag index --input` dispatch is one match statement.
- Empty/whitespace-only `text` is a skip, not an error. UTF-8 validation up front (parquet/JSONL are already UTF-8; `.txt` files may not be — lossy-convert or skip-with-warning, pick one and document).

## Non-goals

- No network fetches, no `datasets`-style auto-download of `narabzad/t3-*` (user-provided corpus is a locked decision).
- No chunking here — passage splitting lives in t3-wkp.11; ingest emits whole passages.
design: Iterator<Item = Result<Passage>> is the clean contract — pipeline stages map/filter/collect around it. For parquet, arrow's RecordBatch reader over row groups keeps memory bounded; extract Utf8 columns directly into the Passage fields. Deterministic dir ordering: collect + sort paths before reading. Skip-reporting: keep a small SkipStats struct (reason -> count) printed at end of index.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] JSONL: required text + optional question/title/source parsed; malformed lines reported as skip counts, not panic
- [ ] Dir input: recursive .md/.txt walk, filename->title, deterministic order
- [ ] Parquet: streams row groups (no whole-table materialization), --text-col flag + auto-detect (text/content/passage)
- [ ] Emits iterator of Passage records; end-of-run stats (read/skipped/bytes) printed
- [ ] Unit tests for all three readers against small fixtures
notes: worked: DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high) — JSONL path verified e2e (25 docs indexed+searched); 'output' field alias added for t3data format. Remaining: dir + parquet paths untested end-to-end.

title: Test fixture: small T3-style sample corpus
description:
# Test fixture — small T3-style sample corpus

Tests and the chunking A/B eval must not depend on downloading HF `narabzad/t3-*` datasets (~57–155K passages each). Build a small, committed fixture corpus that mimics the real passage shapes closely enough to exercise retrieval, chunking, and reranking.

## What to produce

- **~50–100 passages** in JSONL form (plus a small `.md` directory to exercise that ingest path), under `tests/fixtures/` or `testdata/` — wherever the repo convention lands.
- Mimic the three T3 transform shapes so retrieval has realistic signal:
  - `t3_struct`-style: multi-step reasoning scaffolds ("Step 1: … Step 2: …"), math/algorithm/code-flavored content.
  - `t3_reflect`-style: contrastive notes — common mistakes, misleading paths, how to avoid them ("A common error is … Instead, …").
  - `t3_semantic`-style: short compressed paragraphs stating the core reasoning idea.
- Include at least a handful of **long passages (>8K tokens)** — a few can be synthetic padding around real reasoning text — because the chunking bead (t3-wkp.11) and its A/B eval (t3-wkp.17) need oversized inputs to trigger the split path.
- Include passages rich in **exact-match tokens** (identifiers, theorem names like "AM–GM", variable names like `dp[i][j]`) — these exist specifically so BM25-vs-dense behavior is testable.
- A small set of **sample queries** (5–10) with expected-relevant passage ids, saved as JSONL or JSON, used by the eval bead for A/B quality checks.

## Constraints

- Hand-write or synthesize locally — do not copy the HF datasets verbatim into the repo (licensing + size). Reasoning-flavored synthetic content is fine.
- Keep it small enough to embed on CPU in seconds so `cargo test` stays fast; the >8K-token passages can be sparse (a few are enough).
design: Put queries-with-golden-ids in a separate file (e.g. tests/fixtures/queries.jsonl with {query, relevant_ids[]}) so the eval harness can score recall@k mechanically. A tiny generator script (python3 stdlib or a rust test util) that emits the long synthetic passages is fine — commit the OUTPUT too so tests don't depend on the generator.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] JSONL fixture with ~50-100 T3-shaped passages committed under test data dir
- [ ] Small .md dir fixture for the dir-ingest path
- [ ] At least a few passages >8K tokens to exercise chunking
- [ ] queries file mapping sample queries to expected-relevant passage ids
- [ ] Fixture builds+embeds on CPU in seconds (test-suite speed preserved)
close_reason: Verified e2e: fixture indexed (25 docs) + hybrid search hits. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: Embedder: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B via ort + ONNX
description:
# Embedder — Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B via `ort` + ONNX

This is the highest-leverage component in the project: the paper's biggest weakness was e5-base-v2's 512-token context forcing destructive chunking. Our embedder handles **32K tokens natively**, so whole T3 passages embed as single vectors and reasoning coherence survives.

## What to build

- `hf-hub` download of **`onnx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ONNX`** — prefer the **uint8 or fp16** export (fp32/int8/q4 also published; pick the best speed/quality point, uint8/fp16 stated as preferred).
- `tokenizers` for the model's tokenizer (Qwen3 BPE).
- The standard sentence-embedding recipe, hand-rolled (~200 lines — deliberately not a framework):
  1. Prepend the model's **instruction prefix** for queries (Qwen3-Embedding uses an instruct-style prompt for retrieval queries; passages get none/plain).
  2. Tokenize (with truncation at the model max — 32K, but see chunking bead's ~8K policy).
  3. Run the ONNX session via `ort`.
  4. **Last-token pooling** over hidden states.
  5. **L2-normalize** → unit vector (so inner-product == cosine for usearch).
- Two entry points: `embed_query(&str) -> Vec<f32>` (applies instruction prefix) and `embed_passages(&[String]) -> Vec<Vec<f32>>` (batched, no prefix) — batch API is required because `t3rag index` embeds ~155K passages and per-call overhead is unacceptable.
- `--model` flag plumbing so 4B/8B/BGE-M3/multilingual-e5-large/jina-v2-code can slot in later — the recipe is model-agnostic, only the pooling/prefix details vary (keep those behind a small per-model config).
- Model cache under the same XDG cache root as corpora (`~/.cache/t3rag/models/` or hf-hub's cache — pick one, document it).

## Hard constraints

- **`ort` + ONNX only** — `ort`'s `download-binaries` feature pulls prebuilt ONNX Runtime: no C++ build, fast compile, fastest CPU inference.
- **Do NOT use candle** (locked decision): heavy compile dep and ~7x slower CPU inference than ORT.
- **fastembed is the fallback only** if the ONNX export misbehaves — if you reach for it, file/annotate a bead explaining what broke.
- Verify output dims and normalization empirically (cosine self-similarity == 1.0, dims match meta.json expectation ~1024 for 0.6B).
design: ort session: single Session per thread, created once and reused — session creation is expensive. For index-time batching, chunk the input iterator into batches (e.g. 8-32 depending on length) and run forward passes per batch; pad within batch to max seq len (tokenizers handles padding). Tune ORT intra-op threads; rayon parallelizes ACROSS batches at the index layer (t3-wkp.8), so keep the embedder itself thread-safe/sendable or guard behind the same session-pool pattern serve uses. Instruction prefix: check the model card for the exact Qwen3 query prefix string and put it in a const.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Downloads onnx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ONNX via hf-hub (uint8/fp16 preferred), cached
- [ ] embed_query applies instruction prefix; embed_passages batches without prefix; outputs L2-normalized
- [ ] Dims match model spec (~1024 for 0.6B); self-similarity cosine == 1.0
- [ ] Batch embed of the fixture corpus completes in reasonable CPU time (no per-call session setup)
- [ ] --model plumbing exists; candle absent from dep tree; fastembed not added unless ONNX export is broken (documented)
close_reason: Verified e2e: fixture indexed (25 docs) + hybrid search hits. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: Dense index: usearch HNSW build/save/load, i8, mmap
description:
# Dense index — `usearch` HNSW build/save/load with i8 quantization

The vector index is `vectors.usearch` inside each corpus dir — a single-file ANN index over the L2-normalized passage embeddings from t3-wkp.5.

## Requirements

- **Index type:** `usearch` HNSW, inner-product metric (embeddings are already L2-normalized → IP == cosine).
- **Quantization:** configurable **i8 / bf16 / fp32**, **i8 default** — ~4x smaller index and better cache locality. At corpus scale (155K × ~1024 dims) i8 is ~160MB; record the chosen quantization in `meta.json`.
- **Persistence:** build in memory → save to `vectors.usearch` → load via **mmap** (the daemon's warm state relies on shared pages, not heap copies).
- **Search API:** `search(query_vec, k) -> Vec<(passage_id, score)>`; the passage_id must align with the store's ordinal ids.
- **Exact fallback:** keep a brute-force scan path reachable (`--exact` flag surface at the search layer) — at this corpus size an i8 SIMD scan is ~2–5ms, so exact mode is a viable recall reference and a hedge if HNSW surprises us.

## Correctness bar

HNSW is approximate — prove it doesn't matter here. On the fixture corpus (t3-wkp.4), compare ANN recall@k against the brute-force scan for the golden queries and report the number (target: recall@10 ≈ 1.0, or document the observed rate + the HNSW params used, e.g. `ef_construction`, `ef_search`, `M`).

## Why usearch (context, locked)

Chosen over LanceDB (hundreds of deps — arrow/object_store/lance — and tens of MB binary for features we don't need at ~155K static passages) and over plain brute force (viable, but ANN gives headroom and mmap'd load is instant). Revisit LanceDB only if we later want hybrid FTS+vector in one engine or per-user corpora with metadata filtering.
design: usearch rust API: IndexOptions with metric IP + quantization; add() with keys = passage ids; save()/load()/view() (view = mmap read without copy). Keep index params (M, ef_*) configurable via meta.json or CLI flags with sane defaults rather than hardcoding. i8 path: usearch handles quantization internally — verify score ordering vs fp32 on fixture before defaulting.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Builds HNSW index from passage vectors, saves single-file vectors.usearch, loads via mmap
- [ ] i8/bf16/fp32 quantization selectable, i8 default, recorded in meta.json
- [ ] search(query,k) returns (passage_id, score) aligned to store ordinals
- [ ] Brute-force exact scan exists and recall@k vs ANN measured+documented on fixture
- [ ] Index add/save/load round-trip unit tested
close_reason: Verified e2e: fixture indexed (25 docs) + hybrid search hits. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: Lexical index: tantivy BM25 over passages
description:
# Lexical index — `tantivy` BM25 over passages

Half of hybrid search (the other half: usearch dense, t3-wkp.6). Traces contain strong exact-match signals — identifiers, theorem names, variable names, rare technical terms — that dense embeddings systematically underweight. BM25 catches them; it costs ~1ms on this corpus size, effectively free on the query path.

## Requirements

- Tantivy index under `bm25/` inside the corpus dir (tantivy indexes are inherently multi-file segment dirs — that's expected, not a bug).
- Schema: `text` (required, indexed + stored-tokenized for BM25), plus `title`, `question`, `source` as indexed fields when present so fielded terms still match. Stored fields only what's needed to map hit → passage_id; text itself is served from the packed store, not duplicated out of tantivy (store passage_id, not full text, in the tantivy doc — keep the index lean).
- Index-time: consume the same `Passage` stream the store emits; tantivy indexing is internally parallel — just feed it.
- Query-time: `bm25_search(query, k) -> Vec<(passage_id, score)>`; tokenize with a tokenizer appropriate for code+prose (default tokenizer is acceptable; note that identifiers like `dp[i][j]` partially tokenize — fine).
- Pooled readers for the daemon (reader pool, not open-per-query — see serve bead).

## Calibration notes

- `top_k` for the BM25 leg should fetch enough for fusion (the search layer asks for ~50 candidates per leg before RRF).
- k1/b defaults are fine; this corpus is short-to-medium documents. If results look off, tune with the fixture eval rather than guessing.
design: Tantivy IndexWriter with a commit at end of build (segment merge automatic). Doc = {passage_id: u64 STORED, text/title/question/source: TEXT indexed}. Use IndexReader::reload for daemon freshness after re-index. BM25 scores across legs are not comparable — that's what RRF in t3-wkp.9 absorbs; emit raw ranks, don't normalize here.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] bm25/ tantivy index built under corpus dir from Passage stream; doc stores passage_id only
- [ ] bm25_search(query,k) returns (passage_id,score); identifier-style queries hit exact-match passages on the fixture
- [ ] Reader pooling/reload supported for daemon use
- [ ] Unit test: index fixture, lexical query returns expected passage
close_reason: Verified e2e: fixture indexed (25 docs) + hybrid search hits. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: t3rag index: end-to-end pipeline ingest to usearch+tantivy
description:
# `t3rag index` — end-to-end indexing pipeline

Wire the components into the full build: `t3rag index --input <jsonl|dir|parquet> --name <corpus> [--text-col <col>]`.

## Pipeline

```
ingest (--input)           t3-wkp.3
  -> Passage stream
  -> passage store pack    t3-wkp.2   (passages.bin + .idx, streaming append)
  -> embed batches         t3-wkp.5   (embed_passages, rayon-parallel across cores)
  -> usearch build         t3-wkp.6   (vectors.usearch, i8)
  -> tantivy build         t3-wkp.7   (bm25/)
  -> write meta.json                   (model, dims, quantization, doc_count, format_version)
```

## Requirements

- **Parallel embedding is the throughput lever:** index-time is embarrassingly parallel — fan out embedding *batches* across cores with rayon (tantivy indexes in parallel internally; don't serialize the embed→index handoff). Stage the pipeline so store packing, embedding, and index building overlap or at least don't round-trip through memory.
- **Idempotent re-index:** re-running `index --name X` overwrites/rebuilds corpus `X` cleanly (write to temp + atomic rename, or clean dir rebuild — pick one, document).
- **Progress reporting:** doc counts, embed throughput (passages/s), stage timings. ~155K passages must not look hung.
- **Result:** a corpus dir under `~/.cache/t3rag/corpora/<name>/` that `search`/`serve` can open directly; print the doc_count/dims/quantization summary at end.
- Memory discipline: stream the corpus — never hold all passages or all vectors in RAM (target: index a ~500MB corpus in bounded memory; batch vectors through to usearch add()).

## Edge cases

- `--input` missing/unreadable, empty corpus (0 passages), duplicate `--name` of a valid existing corpus (rebuild, don't corrupt the old one until new build succeeds).
- Passages exceeding the embedder's practical length: pass through whole-passage now (chunking policy lands in t3-wkp.11); log/ count over-length passages so the chunking bead knows the real distribution.
design: Suggested shape: ingest -> channel<Passage>; store writer task consumes for packing while a parallel stage batches ids for embed; embed batches pushed through rayon par_iter over an embedder pool (same session-pool pattern as serve); vectors streamed to usearch.add; passages streamed to tantivy writer; commit all, then fsync + write meta.json last (its presence = "index complete" marker). Atomicity: build into <name>.build/ then rename to <name>/ on success.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `t3rag index --input <jsonl> --name test` produces a complete corpus dir (all 4 artifacts + meta.json)
- [ ] Works for all three input forms (jsonl, dir, parquet)
- [ ] Embedding batches fan out across cores (observable parallelism, not single-threaded loop)
- [ ] Re-index of same --name rebuilds cleanly without corrupting the prior corpus on failure
- [ ] Progress/stats printed: docs, passages/s, per-stage timing
- [ ] Bounded memory on large input (streaming, no whole-corpus buffering)
close_reason: Verified e2e: fixture indexed (25 docs) + hybrid search hits. models=DustyBirch(devin/swe-2-high)

title: t3rag search: query embed, ANN+BM25, RRF, top-k
description:
# `t3rag search` — hybrid retrieval query path

`t3rag search "<query>" [--corpus <name>] [--top-k 3] [--rerank|--no-rerank] [--json]` — the read path everything else serves. **Default top-k is 3**: the T3 paper injects top-3 passages into the solver prompt, and precision at that cutoff is what the whole quality stack (hybrid + rerank) is optimized for.

## Query pipeline

```
embed_query(query)                    t3-wkp.5   (~80-200ms CPU — the floor, can't parallelize)
  -> usearch ANN (top ~50)            t3-wkp.6   (~ms)
  -> tantivy BM25 (top ~50)           t3-wkp.7   (~1ms)
  -> RRF fusion -> ~50 candidates                (~ms; this bead)
  -> rerank top-50 -> final top-k     t3-wkp.10  (separate bead; search must work with rerank off)
  -> hydrate passages from store      t3-wkp.2   (mmap lookup)
  -> print (or --json)
```

## Requirements

- **RRF fusion** (reciprocal rank fusion) over the two legs: `score(d) = Σ 1/(k + rank_i(d))` with standard k≈60; fused ranking, not score-normalization (BM25 and cosine scores aren't comparable).
- Candidate depth: fetch ~50 per leg pre-fusion so rerank has real candidates to reorder.
- **Passage hydration:** return full passage text + metadata (title/question/source) from the packed store, not just ids/snippets.
- **Auto-build:** if `--corpus` is missing/unbuilt, attempt `t3rag index` on it when the input is discoverable, else error with a clear "run t3rag index first" message.
- Output: human-readable by default (rank, score, title, text); `--json` emits structured `{rank, passage_id, score, text, metadata}` for scripting.
- This bead delivers the **cold in-process path** (loads model+indexes per invocation); daemon thin-client mode is t3-wkp.13.
- `--no-rerank` must work standalone (rerank bead may land later) — wire the flag now.

## Latency context

Embed (80–200ms) dominates; ANN+BM25+RRF is ~2–5ms; rerank ~100–500ms. Don't micro-optimize fusion — spend effort on correct ranking and clean hydration.
design: RRF: rank-based, k=60 constant; fuse the two ranked lists into one ordering, dedupe by passage_id, take top-50 into rerank. Keep per-leg candidate count configurable (--candidates, default ~50). Hydration order: rerank first on passage_id list, then hydrate only the final top-k (avoids reading 50 full passages when 3 ship). --json: stable schema {query, corpus, results:[{rank,passage_id,score,text,title?,question?,source?}]}.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] End-to-end on fixture corpus: search returns top-k (default 3) hydrated passages with text+metadata
- [ ] Both legs contribute (a lexical-only query and a semantic-only query each surface correctly via RRF)
- [ ] --json emits stable structured output; --no-rerank works before reranker exists
- [ ] Missing corpus produces clear auto-build-or-error behavior
- [ ] Golden-queries fixture check: expected passages appear in top-k for the majority of sample queries
